children: Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd, one of the larger class-action law firms, has sued Delaware Life, Guggenheim Partners and their owner Mark Walter on behalf of a senior citizen who bought an annuity from Delaware Life earlier this year.

The complaint filed in the U.S. district court of Miami, Fla., is one of the first such cases against Walker's financial empire, but others could follow. Hundreds of thousands of Americans bought retirement products from Delaware Life and other insurers Walter owns through parent company Group 1001. Federal investigators are looking into whether Walter or his companies committed fraud by concealing financial connections while borrowing from insurers he controls.

Robbins Geller's lead plaintiff is Ira Rosner, a 67-year-old Miami resident who purchased an annuity from Delaware Life in April with 30-day, no-penalty return. The insurer had already received grand jury subpoenas in February but didn't disclose them until a June regulatory filing, long after Rosner's return window had closed, the complaint alleges.
The lawsuit seeks damages for negligent misrepresentation, breach of contract and aiding and abetting fraud.

A spokesman for Walter didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Walter's conglomerate, TWG Global, has said there was no fraud at either his Wall Street firm Guggenheim Partners or at his insurers.
